title: Spiral rollout orchestration with probe-matrix checks and fallthrough routing lanes
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Goal: implement a 'spiral' rollout primitive that layers A/B slices, shadow probes, and progressive traffic promotion with deterministic fallthrough lanes by region and capacity tier. The spiral flow exercises a probe-matrix for compatibility checks (input shapes, output schema, kv-cache parity, streaming semantics) before live traffic promotion. Fallthrough lanes define ordered routing fallback: local warm-variant -> regional-compatible-variant -> low-cost-quantized-variant -> hosted-fallback. We want deterministic, auditable routing decisions and clear automatic rollback triggers based on end-to-end quality signals and capacity SLO breaches.

Scope: routing policy composer, probe-matrix evaluation engine, fallthrough lane config schema, rollout controller changes, metric hooks for quality SLOs, canary traffic UI in Console, and docs for on-call. Excludes long-term rollout analytics pipeline and cross-customer experiment UI (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can execute a spiral rollout plan with at least 4 discrete stages including shadow-only and live promotion
Probe-matrix runs pre-promotion checks and records pass/fail with reasons in audit log
Router honors fallthrough lanes and prefers regional-compatible variants while respecting capacity tiers
Automatic rollback triggers when aggregated quality delta > 3% absolute or error-rate exceed 5xx baseline by 4x within 10 minutes
Console shows stage, current weights, and top failing probes; can abort/pause from UI
End-to-end test harness reproduces a simulated regional egress failure and validates policy failover sequence
rollout_plan: 1) Create schema for fallthrough lanes and spiral stages (compact DSL). 2) Implement probe-matrix runner that executes a set of lightweight compatibility probes (schema, kv-cache replay, streaming handshake, output type checks). 3) Extend routing-table to attach lane priority and capacity-tier affinity. 4) Add controller state machine: INIT -> SHADOW -> GRADUAL_PROMOTE -> STEADY -> ROLLBACK. 5) Wire metrics: per-probe pass-rate, per-variant p50/p95 latency, token cost, and quality delta from ground truth prompts. 6) Integrate rollback signals and safe-eviction procedure that gracefully drains inflight requests. 7) Expose control in Console canary page. 8) Run closed alpha on infra-team allocation then roll to a single customer sandbox before general availability.
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser and probe runner; integration test that simulates 3-region topology with one degraded region; chaos test exercising capacity-tier eviction; e2e canary run against canary-corp sandbox with synthetic and real prompts; load tests to ensure routing decision latency < 5ms per request. Acceptance test harness located at github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-e2e (PR linked).
metrics_and_rollbacks: Primary signals: quality_delta (measured via golden prompts), 5xx_rate, p95_latency, token_cost_delta. Thresholds: quality_delta > 0.03 absolute OR 5xx_rate > baseline*4 for 10m -> immediate rollback. Soft signals (p95_latency increase <25%) trigger pause and extended shadow stage. Rollback policy will: 1) Abort promotion, 2) Reassign traffic to previous steady variant via fallthrough lanes, 3) Trigger on-call alert and create incident with automatic diagnostics bundle.
failure_modes_and_mitigations: - Probe false-positive: reduce probe weight and require 2 consecutive failures across stages before blocking promotion. - Regional partition: fallthrough lanes prefer cross-region compatible variants; if none, route to hosted-fallback and mark degraded mode. - Capacity spike: throttle new promotions and open burst-tier soft-eviction (prefer quantized-variant). - Schema drift: probes detect structural mismatches and generate clear remediation hints for model owners.
open_questions: What is the canonical set of probes for all model families (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, chat state)?
How to represent lane affinity for Dedicated pools vs Hosted (config granularity)?
Should the spiral plan support multi-axis experiments (simultaneous A/B and quantization)?
What telemetry retention window is required for quick rollback analysis (30d vs 90d)?

2026-02-18 - Mateo Alvarez: Proof-of-concept probe runner finished. Early results show schema and kv-cache probes catch >90% of regressions in synthetic tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4217
2026-02-24 - Priya Singh (PM): Asked to include explicit customer migration guide and an opt-in flag for Dedicated customers. Added to scope as follow-up doc.

2026-03-03 - QA: Integration tests for regional failover added. Found a race when eviction happens during streaming responses; mitigation implemented to drain with soft-evict token fencing. Issue tracked ENG-20456.
2026-03-09 - Security (Ben Kim): Reviewed audit log schema; requested immutability for stage audit records. We'll store signed snapshots in the control plane and include a retention policy.
next_steps: 1) Finalize probe list and DSL grammar (owner: Emily). 2) Merge probe-runner PR and land routing-table adjustments (owner: Mateo). 3) Coordinate Dedicated-team for opt-in hooks and capacity-tier mapping. 4) Schedule alpha with infra-team (target week 2026-03-15).
notes: This ticket intentionally uses different terminology (spiral, fallthrough lanes) to reduce confusion with existing 'canary' and 'shadow' tickets; it focuses on deterministic failover ordering and probe-driven gating rather than traffic-slice heuristics.
